### Key findings
- Storage is already closer than the UI docs to a normalized record family model.

- `storage-plan.md` already defines several canonical records (attempt_record, tier_runtime_record, blocked_projection, usage_record, evidence_record, thread_blocked_notice, wizard_runtime_state, cross-surface runtime receipt record).
- `Contracts_V0.md` consistently uses: `detail_ref?`, `*_ref`, explicit identity fields, canonical event fields instead of GUI-only aliases.
- The rewrite now wants many additional first-class record families: concerns, reviews, corroboration requests/results, promotions, graph patch requests/results, recovery records.
- What is still missing is a shared envelope pattern that keeps those families structurally compatible.
### Recommended normalization direction
- Strong recommendation: add one shared governance/runtime record-envelope pattern, then let each family add its own payload block.

- Good base envelope fields include: record_id, record_kind, schema_version, project_id, run_id?, scope_type, scope_id, status, created_at_utc, updated_at_utc?, summary, summary_kind?, detail_ref?, source_refs[], artifact_refs[], related_record_refs[], lineage_refs[], actor_ref?, requested_effective_snapshot_refs?.
### Record vs artifact distinction
- Important rule: record and artifact must remain different objects.
- record: structured canonical object used by projections, search, history, and ledger; artifact: blob/file/renderable output linked from a record.
- Separate exact structured record vs human-readable rendered summary vs attached artifact(s) for review/patch output language.
### Family-specific payload direction
- Good pattern: shared envelope + family payload block (concern, promotion, corroboration, graph patch, recovery, review payloads).
### UI / search implication
- A normalized envelope simplifies object-first search, History vs Ledger distinction, deep-link routing, export manifests, cross-tab inspectors.
- Search can index shared envelope fields while preserving family-specific filters; Ledger can inspect record structure consistently across families.
### Historical semantics implication
- Shared envelopes help apply semantic vocabulary consistently: historical, superseded, revoked, reopened, archived, removed — without collapsing to one generic old-state bit.
### Contradictions / gaps surfaced
- Newer governance families risk being invented ad hoc; without a shared envelope, search/export/ledger/deep links will re-encode the same concepts repeatedly.
### Candidate fixes to carry forward
- Define a shared record-envelope contract; keep artifacts/rendered summaries linked but separate; require new Orchestrator families to reuse envelope and status/lineage conventions.
### Do-not-forget details
- Expand (not replace) `detail_ref` and `*_ref` conventions; prose summaries must resolve back to exact records; envelope must support search/export/routing without flattening family meaning.
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Lane / Worktree Cleanup Lifecycle
### Targeted docs read — WorktreeGitImprovement, GitHub_Integration, storage-plan, Orchestrator_Page, FinalGUISpec

- Cleanup is not a trivial delete: worktree rows expose recover/prune/lineage; active-run ownership visible before prune/remove; preserve safe-point/remediation lineage; dirty_worktree and worktree_conflict are blocked reasons.
- WorktreeGitImprovement: conflict worktrees may survive until resolution; recovery across restart; safe-point restore targets exact worktree/baseline.
- Missing full lifecycle separating logical lane history, live worktree existence, cleanup eligibility, archive/remove semantics.
### Recommended lifecycle split
- Treat lane lifecycle and worktree lifecycle as related but non-identical (lane may stay historically important after worktree removed; worktree may be suspect while lane still active).
- Mental model: lane = orchestration lineage object; worktree = concrete Git/filesystem backing object.
### Recommended lane-oriented states
- Lane states: baseline, active, suspect, restoring, retained, cleanup_eligible, archived, removed, historical (with interpretations for dispatch vs historical posture).
### Worktree-oriented state implication
- Worktree-first vocabulary for Source Control: live, dirty, conflict, orphaned, recovering, retained, archived, removed; Orchestrator shows lane state with worktree status in context.
### Cleanup-action semantics
- Important rule: `recover`, `archive`, `prune`, and `remove` must not blur together.

- recover / archive / prune / remove meanings: restore/reconcile vs retire with lineage vs policy-eligible cleanup vs destructive removal after checks; historical record must survive archive/prune/remove.
### Eligibility / gating direction

- Cleanup must be gated by more than age (no active-run ownership; no unresolved blocked recovery on that worktree; no safe-point restore targeting it; no needed conflict workflow; no dependent lineage needing live worktree).
- If gates fail, remain retained/suspect/restoring — not cleanup_eligible.
### Trigger direction
- Transitions to cleanup_eligible vs retained (completion, supersession, revoked/reopened, recovery complete; vs pending review, weak integration, concerns/corroboration, manual retention).
### Source Control vs Orchestrator boundary
- Orchestrator owns lane-pool truth and cleanup posture; Source Control owns concrete worktree actions and compact inventory (filters for retained, cleanup-eligible, archived/removed).
### Historical-lineage rule
- Live cleanup must never erase run/lane/worktree lineage from History, Ledger, or graph-linked inspection.
### Confirmation / undo implication
- archive light/strong; prune/remove usually strong; remove with blocked/recovery lineage may approach hard_gate; recovery via compensating action/metadata not generic undo.
### Contradictions / gaps surfaced — lane/worktree cleanup lifecycle not fully defined; cross-surface meanings still fuzzy.
### Candidate fixes — distinct lane/worktree states; eligibility from runtime/recovery/lineage; preserve historical records; Source Control compact with historical behind filters.
### Do-not-forget — visible active-run ownership; safe-point/recovery lineage can keep worktree relevant; cleanup reduces clutter without erasing history.
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Terminology / Help / Glossary Impact Sweep
### Targeted docs read — Glossary, FinalGUISpec, Personas, Models_System, Multi-Account
- Runtime-selection vocabulary (requested vs effective, selection_reason, Persona controls) is ahead of Orchestrator object vocabulary; Glossary.md lags rewrite research.

- Terms needing glossary ownership: Feature Seam, Work Package, Node, overseers, Weak Integration, Promotion, Corroboration, Graph Patch/Generation, Concern, Lane/Lane Pool, Worktree, Historical Run, Reopened/Revoked/Superseded, stale_historical, projection trust (current/refreshing/stale/degraded/unavailable).

- High-risk word pairs needing distinction rules: lane vs worktree; record vs artifact; history vs ledger; requested vs effective; override vs requested; current vs historical; historical vs superseded; resolved vs dismissed vs acknowledged; safe point vs fresh attempt; archive vs remove vs prune.
- Glossary owns short definitions; help owns depth; contextual help must not mutate semantics; strong help-entry candidates listed (Weak Integration, Corroboration, Graph Patch, etc.).
- Multi-Account/Models_System/Personas align on requested/effective, selection reason, skipped controls, attempt snapshotting — lower conceptual rewrite risk than Orchestrator/glossary surfaces.
- FinalGUISpec needs cross-cutting copy discipline to avoid casual retry/old/completed/degraded/history wording where canonical terms are required.
### Contradictions — Glossary behind Orchestrator vocabulary; copy drift risk in Orchestrator tabs, Source Control, blocked/recovery, concerns/promotions/patches labels.
### Candidate fixes — expand Glossary; use it as canonical short-definition source; add distinction guidance; re-check FinalGUISpec for informal synonyms.
### Do-not-forget — do not reinvent requested/effective; glossary/help before UI copy crystallizes; lane vs worktree, history vs ledger, historical vs superseded are drift-prone.
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Shared Conversational-Actor / Runtime Identity Boundary
### Targeted docs read — assistant-chat-design, interview-subagent-integration, chain-wizard-flexibility, FinalGUISpec, Multi-Account, Personas, Models_System
- Shared provider-runtime contract applies beyond Orchestrator (assistant, interviewer, builders, overseers, node workers, provider-backed chat); requested/effective and selection reason are shared.
- Conversational/document-production surfaces require effective Persona, selection reason, platform/model, skipped-control disclosure (Interview, Requirements Builder, subagent blocks).
- Shared failure/remediation taxonomy: failure_class/blocked_reason_code; chat blocked notices use allowed_action_ids[] and canonical metadata.

### Main boundary clarification — conversational actors share provider/runtime identity semantics but are not orchestration execution objects (not Feature Seams, Work Packages, Nodes, lane-pool, package/seam governance).
### Identity-model direction — distinct families: thread_id; wizard_id/stage/bundle ids; run_id/package/seam/node/attempt ids — linkable but not collapsed.
### Shared-runtime surface parity — multiple surfaces showing the same active conversational/document-production run must share underlying runtime state and requested/effective fields.
### Blocked-state implication — blocked not Orchestrator-exclusive; attention_required/blocked/blocked_reason_code/allowed_action_ids/resume_url across Chat/Interview/Wizard.
### Non-goal / anti-drift — shared provider runtime does not imply shared execution ontology (same machinery, different object families and lifecycles).
### Search / record implication — span actors without flattening; shared runtime-identity fields with distinct actor/run kinds (assistant, interview, builder, orchestrator).
### Contradictions — 'shared runtime, separate ontology' mostly implicit; risk of over-unifying or duplicating identity logic.
### Candidate fixes — explicit boundary statement; preserve actor/run kinds; one disclosure grammar; shared blocked taxonomy with actor-specific state machines.
### Do-not-forget — thread_id, wizard_id, bundle/review ids, orchestration ids linkable but distinct; blocked notices prove shared taxonomy without shared ontology.
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Export Contracts
### Targeted docs read — usage-feature, FinalGUISpec, Orchestrator_Page, storage-plan, Runtime_Artifacts_Panel, chain-wizard-flexibility

- Export families: .pm-bundle; render exports; Artifacts panel export; Usage/Ledger CSV/JSON; project outputs under .puppet-master/project/**; seglog/JSONL history — no unified Orchestrator export contract yet.
- Runtime_Artifacts_Panel: canonical runtime identity; Show in Ledger/Usage; no shadow models. chain-wizard: sharded graph canonical, monolithic export derived.
- Orchestrator_Page export language thin: filtered ledger export but weak run/evidence/history/record-bundle contract.
### Recommended export taxonomy — record export vs bundle export vs view export (exact records vs portable multi-record manifest vs filtered/rendered outputs).

### Orchestrator-specific export candidates — records (concern, promotion, corroboration, patch, recovery, ledger slice); bundles (evidence, selected objects, historical run package); views (CSV/JSON tables, search, graph render).

### Manifest direction — non-trivial bundle exports should carry manifest (export_id, export_kind, schema_version, project_id, focused_run_id?, source_surface, generated_at_utc, filter_summary?, included_record_ids[], included_artifact_ids[]).
- Manifest fields continued: included_file_paths[]?, lineage_notes?, trust_state_at_export? (important given stale/degraded projections).

### Canonical-vs-derived rule — export convenience must not redefine canonical truth (CSV view ≠ canonical history; JSON summary ≠ record export unless exact envelope; monolithic graph derived; JSONL mirror projection-derived).
### Runtime-artifact implication — preserve run/thread/attempt linkage; no shadow IDs; usage artifacts route through canonical usage identity.
### Trust / stale-data implication — exports from stale/degraded projections must disclose trust in manifest or re-query canonical backing (ledger, concerns, promotions, graph generation).
### Retention / archival — export supports long-term retention; may motivate cleanup transitions but does not authorize deleting canonical/historical records.
### Contradictions — no single Orchestrator export contract tying records, artifacts, manifests, view exports, trust disclosure; JSON export meaning ambiguous.
### Candidate fixes — define record/bundle/view taxonomy; require manifests; preserve canonical ids/refs; trust disclosure or revalidation for projection-based exports.
### Do-not-forget — do not blur export families; filtered JSON ≠ canonical record export; derived exports must stay visibly derived.
## Research Progress - 2026-03-16 - Notifications / Escalation Interaction with Concerns, Blocked Ownership, and Projection Trust
### Targeted docs read — FinalGUISpec, Orchestrator_Page, usage-feature, assistant-chat-design, interview-subagent-integration

- Escalation ladder: info, warning, attention_required, blocked, system_notification; blocked vs attention_required distinct; wizard-blocked outranks attention-required; usage quiet periods; all-nodes-blocked time escalation.
- Missing interaction policy: concern state × escalation; blocked-owner routing; stale/degraded trust qualifying notifications.
### Concern interaction — severity alone does not drive escalation; combine severity, execution impact, persistence, ownership; acknowledged must not mask active blocked.
### Blocked-owner interaction — owner shapes destination surface and notification style (User vs overseers vs Runtime/Recovery/Graph Patch vs External Resource).
### Projection-trust interaction — stale/degraded projections must not drive overconfident notifications; prefer canonical events/blocked records over untrusted rollups.
### Routing / surface model — History (chronology), Progress/Dashboard (active attention), thread/chat (user action), system notification (sparse high-value).
### Resurfacing — good triggers: severity increase, owner change, advisory→execution impact, blocked duration, trust state changes; bad: identical stale heartbeat summaries.
### Usage / pressure — quiet periods for threshold warnings must not hide canonical blocked/action-needed episodes.
### Copy / severity — qualify copy for trust (stale/degraded patterns vs strong claims from untrusted projections).
### Contradictions — notification interaction layer incomplete; risks over-notify, misroute, confident alerts from degraded projections.

### Candidate fixes — route on severity, execution impact, blocked owner, persistence, projection trust; acknowledgment as noise control only; quiet windows not for unresolved blocked; stale/degraded disclosure before strong claims.
### Do-not-forget — blocked owner drives where/how user is notified; projection trust affects confidence; acknowledgment cannot fake health under blocked runtime.
